subject: Performance handshake: parallelism & rate negotiation with FastPay
body:
From: Samir Shah <samir@fastpay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj@fastpay.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FastPay - follow-up: concurrency targets & streaming

Marcus — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from my side and a few open questions so we can move the pilot/quote forward.

High-level requirements (from our ops + product):
- Peak concurrent requests: ~120 parallel in steady-state, with short spikes up to ~240 for 60-90s during batch settlement windows.
- Average request size: 350 tokens in, 150 tokens out; a subset of flows stream incremental results (transaction-line aggregation) and need low first-byte latency.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 220ms for non-streaming responses; streaming needs first-chunk <= 120ms.
- Throughput: steady 900 requests/min (15 rps) with occasional bursts ramping to ~60 rps during peak windows.
- Connection reuse: we expect 50+ frontend workers making persistent HTTP/2 connections from two regions (us-east, us-west). We want guidance on connection pooling and recommended per-connection QPS limits.

Ask from FastPay: can you confirm Redwood's per-tenant rate limits, connection pooling guidance, and recommended Dedicated sizing to meet the targets above? Also please attach any sample quota sheets you use for sizing and a preliminary estimate so we can review before procurement.

I attached our internal summary (fastpay-requested-qps-sla.pdf) — it has a short diagram of our request distribution.

Thanks,
Samir Shah
Head of Platform
FastPay

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@fastpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FastPay - follow-up: concurrency targets & streaming

Samir — great to sync. Appreciate the clear numbers. Looping in Neha (solutions/SE) and Monica (CS / procurement) to get a fast sizing + quote.

Quick notes / clarifying Qs from Redwood:
- Tokens per request: you noted 350/150 avg. Can you confirm the 350 is the input prompt tokens or includes system/context tokens? Helps for exact token-rate calc.
- Streaming split: what percent of requests require streaming? If it's small (<= 10%), we can route those to a streaming-optimized pool; otherwise we should size for mixed workloads.
- Region split: do you expect even traffic from us-east/us-west or ~70/30? A small imbalance changes where we recommend capacity.
- Can you share the number of persistent worker processes that will create connections (not just frontend requests) — that helps with recommended max concurrent connections.

Planned next steps: Neha will draft a sizing worksheet and show two recommended options — 1) Dedicated pool tuned for latency (canary capacity + autoscale for spikes) and 2) Hosted with a hybrid rate-tier + streaming fallback. We'll include per-connection guidance. Monica will follow up on procurement timeline / DocuSign.

Neha — can you take the numbers and attach an initial quota sheet? Please include recommended per-connection QPS, suggested connection pool size, and a cost estimate ballpark.

Samir — we'll aim to get a first-pass worksheet by EOD PT today (or latest by tomorrow morning). Would you prefer a short call Tuesday to finalize?

— Marcus
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Samir Shah <samir@fastpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 13:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FastPay - follow-up: concurrency targets & streaming

Samir / Marcus — attaching a preliminary sizing worksheet (proposed_quota_sheet.xlsx) and a quick topology sketch (network-topology.png). High level takeaways from our calc:

Sizing assumptions used:
- Effective tokens per request (model-side): 520 tokens (includes system/context overhead) — aligns to your 350/150 split plus ~20% system/context.
- Average token generation throughput: 200 tokens/sec per GPU thread (conservative for Redwood-verified medium LLMs on T4v3-like instances); streaming first-chunk latency dominated by network + service WARM path.
- Target 95th latency <= 220ms requires a warm steady-state connection pool with short queueing; aim to keep per-GPU concurrent generation fanout low (<= 6 active requests/GPU) for the requested model profile.

Preliminary recommendations:
1) Dedicated option (recommended for predictability):
   - Start with a 4-GPU pool (model partitioning + KV cache) with autoscale to 8 GPUs for burst handling. This maps to ~120 steady concurrent requests with headroom for 240 spikes when autoscaled.
   - Connection guidance: allocate 12 persistent HTTP/2 connections per region (each connection can safely carry 10-12 concurrent streams given our runtime optimizations). That maps to 120-144 concurrent streams per region; with your 50 worker processes we recommend connection reuse per worker (2-3 streams/worker).
   - Rate limiting: apply a tenant-level soft limit at 300 rps with hard limit at 400 rps for short bursts; this protects latency SLOs and enables graceful shedding.

2) Hosted + hybrid streaming (lower upfront cost):
   - Use hosted API with reserved rate tier: configure a streaming-optimized route for first-chunk SLOs (prioritized lanes) and place non-streaming traffic on standard lanes. Recommended reserved rate: 200 rps with spike allowance to 400 rps.
   - If streaming requests >15% of traffic, prefer Dedicated — the streaming lanes consume slot capacity quickly and increase tail latency on shared pools.

Other notes / tradeoffs:
- Kernel scheduling: to keep 95th low we throttle batching size for low-latency routes (sacrifices some cost efficiency). We included estimated token cost in the worksheet.
- Fallbacks: suggest a policy to fallback streaming requests to standard responses (non-streamed) if the streaming pool is saturated; Redwood can configure an automatic fallback with an alert.

Action items:
- Marcus / Monica: confirm procurement path (DocuSign vs PO).
- Samir: confirm percent streaming and region split (us-east/us-west).
- Jordan: please prepare a short notes doc with the technical gating items we should validate during the pilot (network egress rules, TLS handshakes, KMS if you need encryption at rest).

Attaching: proposed_quota_sheet.xlsx, network-topology.png.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

---

From: Samir Shah <samir@fastpay.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Raj Patel <raj@fastpay.com>
Date: Sat, 05 Dec 2026 15:08:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: FastPay - follow-up: concurrency targets & streaming

Neha — this is great, thanks for the detail and the worksheet. A few quick replies inline: 

> Effective tokens per request (model-side): 520 tokens
That aligns with our internal numbers (350 prompt + ~150 response + embeddings overhead). Good to know you included system/context.

> Connection guidance: allocate 12 persistent HTTP/2 connections per region
We can provision that from our side — our infra team will ensure worker pooling matches that. Can you confirm how Redwood enforces per-connection QPS in the hosted option? We need a deterministic way to map worker processes -> expected success rate during spikes.

> Rate limiting: soft 300 rps, hard 400 rps
That seems reasonable. Can you provide a short bullet we can include in our SOW that explains behavioral outcome when soft limit is hit (e.g., queuing, token-drop, 429s with retry-after)? We’ll need to present that to our reliability team.

Next steps for us:
- Internal procurement prefers a short call on Tue (12/8) at 10:00am PT to finalize the quote and get an initial DocuSign draft.
- We'll also share our expected percent streaming by Monday EOD (should be ~12%).

If you can include the SOW bullet and a first-pass price band in the worksheet, we can fast-track. Thanks again — this is moving quickly on our side.

— Samir
Head of Platform, FastPay
